## 1. How animation works

Animation on a canvas works like a flipbook. Many times per second, you:

1. **Clear** the canvas
2. **Update** your objects (move them, check collisions, etc.)
3. **Draw** everything in its new position

Each of these is one **frame**. Most screens show 60 frames per second.

---

## 2. Your first animation loop

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById("game")
const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")

let x = 0

function loop() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)

  x += 2

  ctx.fillStyle = "purple"
  ctx.fillRect(x, 175, 50, 50)

  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

`requestAnimationFrame(loop)` means: "Browser, next time you're about to update the screen, call `loop` once."

It only calls `loop` **once**. That's why `loop` asks again at the end every time. Each frame schedules the next one.

Why not `setInterval(loop, 16)`? `requestAnimationFrame`:

- runs exactly when the screen is ready to update, so it's smoother
- pauses automatically when you switch to another tab, so it doesn't waste battery

**Question:** what happens if you delete the `clearRect` line?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

The old squares never get erased, so the square leaves a purple smear across the screen.

</details>

**Question:** what happens if you write `loop()` instead of `requestAnimationFrame(loop)` at the end of the function?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

`loop` calls itself immediately, forever, without ever giving the browser a chance to draw. The page freezes, and eventually you get `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.

</details>

---

## 3. Update and draw

As your app grows, keep the **logic** and the **drawing** in separate functions:

```js
function update() {
  // move things, check collisions, update score
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  // draw everything
}

function loop() {
  update()
  draw()
  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

Why bother?

- `update()` never touches `ctx`. `draw()` never changes positions. When something's wrong, you know where to look.
- Pausing becomes easy: skip `update()` but keep calling `draw()`.

---

## 4. Velocity and bouncing

Instead of `x += 2`, give the object a **velocity**: how much it moves per frame in each direction.

```js
const ball = { x: 100, y: 100, vx: 3, vy: 2, radius: 20 }

function update() {
  ball.x += ball.vx
  ball.y += ball.vy

  if (ball.x - ball.radius < 0 || ball.x + ball.radius > canvas.width) {
    ball.vx *= -1
  }
  if (ball.y - ball.radius < 0 || ball.y + ball.radius > canvas.height) {
    ball.vy *= -1
  }
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  ctx.beginPath()
  ctx.arc(ball.x, ball.y, ball.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
  ctx.fillStyle = "tomato"
  ctx.fill()
}
```

- `vx` positive = moving right, negative = moving left.
- `vy` positive = moving **down**, negative = moving **up**.
- `vx *= -1` reverses direction.

Why `ball.x - ball.radius`? Because `ball.x` is the center. The left edge of the ball is `x - radius`, the right edge is `x + radius`.

**A bug you'll eventually see:** sometimes a ball gets stuck in a wall, shaking back and forth. It went so far past the wall that after flipping `vx`, it's still past the wall next frame, so it flips back again. The fix is to push it back inside and force the direction:

```js
if (ball.x - ball.radius < 0) {
  ball.x = ball.radius
  ball.vx = Math.abs(ball.vx)          // always positive = go right
}
if (ball.x + ball.radius > canvas.width) {
  ball.x = canvas.width - ball.radius
  ball.vx = -Math.abs(ball.vx)         // always negative = go left
}
```

## 5. Delta time

There's a hidden problem with "move 3 pixels per frame". Some screens run at 60 frames per second, others at 120 or 144. On a 144Hz screen, `loop` runs 144 times per second, so everything moves more than twice as fast.

The fix: measure **how much time passed** since the last frame, and move by **pixels per second** instead of pixels per frame.

`requestAnimationFrame` gives your function the current time in milliseconds:

```js
let lastTime = null

function loop(time) {
  if (lastTime === null) {
    lastTime = time
  }
  const dt = (time - lastTime) / 1000   // seconds since last frame
  lastTime = time

  update(dt)
  draw()
  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

`dt` ("delta time") is about `0.016` at 60fps and about `0.007` at 144fps.

Now speeds are in **pixels per second**, and you multiply by `dt`:

```js
const ball = { x: 100, y: 100, vx: 200, vy: 150, radius: 20 }

function update(dt) {
  ball.x += ball.vx * dt
  ball.y += ball.vy * dt
}
```

The ball moves 200 pixels per second to the right, on any screen.

**Question:** you switch to another tab for 10 seconds, then come back. `requestAnimationFrame` was paused that whole time. What happens on the first frame back?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

`dt` is about 10 seconds, so the ball moves 2000 pixels in one frame. It teleports, maybe straight through a wall. The fix is to cap `dt`:

```js
const dt = Math.min((time - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1)
```

Now a single frame can never count as more than 0.1 seconds.

</details>

If your test doesn't care about this, pixels-per-frame is fine. But know what `dt` is, because it's the "proper" way and examiners like to see it.

## 6. Classes in the loop

Put lessons 1 and 2 together: each object has `update(dt)` and `draw(ctx)`. The loop calls them on everything.

```js
class Ball {
  constructor(x, y, vx, vy, radius, color) {
    this.x = x
    this.y = y
    this.vx = vx
    this.vy = vy
    this.radius = radius
    this.color = color
  }

  update(dt) {
    this.x += this.vx * dt
    this.y += this.vy * dt
    // bouncing goes here
  }

  draw(ctx) {
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(this.x, this.y, this.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    ctx.fillStyle = this.color
    ctx.fill()
  }
}

const balls = [
  new Ball(100, 100, 200, 150, 20, "tomato"),
  new Ball(300, 200, -120, 80, 30, "teal")
]

function update(dt) {
  for (const ball of balls) {
    ball.update(dt)
  }
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  for (const ball of balls) {
    ball.draw(ctx)
  }
}
```

## 7. Keyboard input

The obvious way to move a player is to change their position inside `keydown`. **Don't.** When you hold a key, the browser sends one `keydown`, waits half a second, then repeats. Movement is jerky, and you can't hold two keys at once (for diagonal movement).

Instead, keep track of **which keys are held down right now**, and check that in `update()`:

```js
const keys = {}

window.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  keys[e.key] = true
})

window.addEventListener("keyup", (e) => {
  keys[e.key] = false
})

const player = { x: 275, y: 175, size: 50, speed: 300 }

function update(dt) {
  if (keys["ArrowLeft"])  player.x -= player.speed * dt
  if (keys["ArrowRight"]) player.x += player.speed * dt
  if (keys["ArrowUp"])    player.y -= player.speed * dt
  if (keys["ArrowDown"])  player.y += player.speed * dt
}
```

`keys` ends up looking like `{ ArrowLeft: true, ArrowUp: false, a: true }`.

Some useful `e.key` values: `"ArrowLeft"`, `"ArrowRight"`, `"ArrowUp"`, `"ArrowDown"`, `" "` (space), `"a"`, `"w"`, `"Enter"`, `"Escape"`. If you're not sure, `console.log(e.key)` and press the key.

### Keeping the player on the screen

`Math.max` and `Math.min` keep a number between two limits ("clamping"):

```js
player.x = Math.max(0, Math.min(player.x, canvas.width - player.size))
```

Read it from the inside out: "no bigger than `canvas.width - player.size`, and no smaller than `0`."

If the arrow keys scroll the page, add `e.preventDefault()` in the `keydown` listener.

## 8. Spawning and removing objects

To create a new enemy every second, use a timer that counts up with `dt`:

```js
let enemies = []
let spawnTimer = 0

function update(dt) {
  spawnTimer += dt
  if (spawnTimer >= 1) {
    enemies.push(new Enemy())
    spawnTimer = 0
  }

  for (const enemy of enemies) {
    enemy.update(dt)
  }

  // remove enemies that fell off the bottom
  enemies = enemies.filter(enemy => enemy.y < canvas.height + 50)
}
```

Use `filter` to remove things. Don't use `splice` inside a `for...of` loop over the same array: removing an item shifts everything after it, and the loop skips the next item.

---

## 9. Collisions

### Rectangle vs rectangle

Two rectangles overlap if they overlap on **both** the x axis and the y axis:

```js
function rectsOverlap(a, b) {
  return a.x < b.x + b.width &&
         a.x + a.width > b.x &&
         a.y < b.y + b.height &&
         a.y + a.height > b.y
}
```

Draw two rectangles on paper and check each line. It's worth understanding, not just copying.

### Circle vs circle

Two circles overlap if the distance between their centers is less than the two radii added together:

```js
function circlesOverlap(a, b) {
  return Math.hypot(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y) < a.radius + b.radius
}
```

### Circle vs rectangle

The exact math is annoying. For most games it's fine to pretend the circle is a square (`x - radius` to `x + radius`) and use the rectangle check.

---

## 10. Game states: playing, paused, game over

Keep a variable that says what the game is doing:

```js
let state = "playing"   // "playing", "paused" or "gameover"

function update(dt) {
  if (state !== "playing") return
  // ...normal game logic
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  // ...draw everything

  if (state === "paused") {
    ctx.fillStyle = "black"
    ctx.font = "40px sans-serif"
    ctx.textAlign = "center"
    ctx.fillText("PAUSED", canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2)
  }
}
```

The loop keeps running the whole time. When paused, `update` does nothing, so nothing moves, but `draw` still shows the frozen game with "PAUSED" on top.

To restart, write a `restart()` function that sets every game variable back to its starting value, and call it once at the beginning too. Then restarting is just `restart()`.

### Stopping the loop completely

`requestAnimationFrame` returns an id. `cancelAnimationFrame(id)` cancels it:

```js
let frameId = requestAnimationFrame(loop)
// inside loop: frameId = requestAnimationFrame(loop)

cancelAnimationFrame(frameId)
```

**Question:** you have a "Start" button that calls `requestAnimationFrame(loop)`. The user clicks it twice. What happens?

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

Now **two** loops are running. Every frame, `update` is called twice, so everything moves twice as fast. Click three times and it's three times as fast.

Fix: keep a `running` variable and only start the loop if it isn't already running. Or start the loop once when the page loads and use `state` to control what happens.

</details>

## 11. Challenges

### Challenge 1: Wrap around

A square moves from left to right. When it goes off the right edge, it comes back in from the left.

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById("game")
const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")

const size = 50
let x = 0

function loop() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)

  x += 3
  if (x > canvas.width) {
    x = -size
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = "purple"
  ctx.fillRect(x, 175, size, size)

  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

Setting `x = -size` (not `0`) makes it slide in smoothly instead of popping in.

</details>

### Challenge 2: Bouncing balls

1. Make a `Ball` class with `update(dt)` and `draw(ctx)`. The ball bounces off all four walls (use the "stuck in the wall" fix from section 4).
2. Use delta time.
3. Make 20 balls with random positions, random speeds (-300 to 300 pixels per second), random sizes and random colors.

Hint: write a helper `function random(min, max) { return Math.random() * (max - min) + min }`

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById("game")
const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")

function random(min, max) {
  return Math.random() * (max - min) + min
}

class Ball {
  constructor() {
    this.radius = random(10, 30)
    this.x = random(this.radius, canvas.width - this.radius)
    this.y = random(this.radius, canvas.height - this.radius)
    this.vx = random(-300, 300)
    this.vy = random(-300, 300)
    this.color = `hsl(${random(0, 360)}, 80%, 50%)`
  }

  update(dt) {
    this.x += this.vx * dt
    this.y += this.vy * dt

    if (this.x - this.radius < 0) {
      this.x = this.radius
      this.vx = Math.abs(this.vx)
    }
    if (this.x + this.radius > canvas.width) {
      this.x = canvas.width - this.radius
      this.vx = -Math.abs(this.vx)
    }
    if (this.y - this.radius < 0) {
      this.y = this.radius
      this.vy = Math.abs(this.vy)
    }
    if (this.y + this.radius > canvas.height) {
      this.y = canvas.height - this.radius
      this.vy = -Math.abs(this.vy)
    }
  }

  draw(ctx) {
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(this.x, this.y, this.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    ctx.fillStyle = this.color
    ctx.fill()
  }
}

const balls = []
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
  balls.push(new Ball())
}

function update(dt) {
  for (const ball of balls) {
    ball.update(dt)
  }
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  for (const ball of balls) {
    ball.draw(ctx)
  }
}

let lastTime = null

function loop(time) {
  if (lastTime === null) {
    lastTime = time
  }
  const dt = Math.min((time - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1)
  lastTime = time

  update(dt)
  draw()
  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

</details>

### Challenge 3: Move the player

A 50×50 square that you move with the arrow keys **and** WASD.

- Smooth movement using the `keys` object from section 7.
- Holding two keys moves diagonally.
- The square can't leave the canvas.

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById("game")
const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")

const keys = {}
window.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  keys[e.key] = true
})
window.addEventListener("keyup", (e) => {
  keys[e.key] = false
})

const player = { x: 275, y: 175, size: 50, speed: 300 }

function update(dt) {
  if (keys["ArrowLeft"] || keys["a"])  player.x -= player.speed * dt
  if (keys["ArrowRight"] || keys["d"]) player.x += player.speed * dt
  if (keys["ArrowUp"] || keys["w"])    player.y -= player.speed * dt
  if (keys["ArrowDown"] || keys["s"])  player.y += player.speed * dt

  player.x = Math.max(0, Math.min(player.x, canvas.width - player.size))
  player.y = Math.max(0, Math.min(player.y, canvas.height - player.size))
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  ctx.fillStyle = "steelblue"
  ctx.fillRect(player.x, player.y, player.size, player.size)
}

let lastTime = null

function loop(time) {
  if (lastTime === null) {
    lastTime = time
  }
  const dt = Math.min((time - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1)
  lastTime = time

  update(dt)
  draw()
  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

Note: with Caps Lock on, `e.key` is `"A"` instead of `"a"`, so WASD stops working. You could fix that with `keys[e.key.toLowerCase()]`, but then the arrow keys become `"arrowleft"`, so you'd have to change those checks too.

</details>

### Challenge 4: Gravity

Click anywhere to drop a ball from that point.

- Gravity: every frame, add to the ball's `vy`. Try `vy += 1500 * dt`.
- When it hits the floor, it bounces back up, but loses some energy. Try `vy *= -0.7`.
- Each ball disappears after 5 seconds. (Give each ball an `age` that goes up by `dt` every frame.)

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById("game")
const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")

const GRAVITY = 1500

class Ball {
  constructor(x, y) {
    this.x = x
    this.y = y
    this.vy = 0
    this.radius = 15
    this.color = `hsl(${Math.random() * 360}, 80%, 50%)`
    this.age = 0
  }

  update(dt) {
    this.vy += GRAVITY * dt
    this.y += this.vy * dt
    this.age += dt

    if (this.y + this.radius > canvas.height) {
      this.y = canvas.height - this.radius
      this.vy *= -0.7
    }
  }

  draw(ctx) {
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(this.x, this.y, this.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    ctx.fillStyle = this.color
    ctx.fill()
  }
}

let balls = []

canvas.addEventListener("click", (e) => {
  const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect()
  balls.push(new Ball(e.clientX - rect.left, e.clientY - rect.top))
})

function update(dt) {
  for (const ball of balls) {
    ball.update(dt)
  }
  balls = balls.filter(ball => ball.age < 5)
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  for (const ball of balls) {
    ball.draw(ctx)
  }
}

let lastTime = null

function loop(time) {
  if (lastTime === null) {
    lastTime = time
  }
  const dt = Math.min((time - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1)
  lastTime = time

  update(dt)
  draw()
  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

</details>

### Challenge 5: Catch game (test practice)

This one puts everything together. Treat it like the real test: plan first, then build it step by step, and test after every step.

**The game:**

- A paddle at the bottom of the screen. Left/right arrow keys move it. It can't leave the canvas.
- Every second, a ball appears at a random x position at the top and falls down.
- Catch a ball with the paddle: +1 score.
- A ball reaches the bottom without being caught: -1 life.
- You start with 3 lives. At 0 lives, the game ends and shows "Game over" with the score.
- Press **P** to pause and unpause.
- Press **R** on the game over screen to restart.
- Show the score and lives in the top-left corner.

**Suggested plan:**

1. Set up the loop with `update(dt)` and `draw()`. Check that it runs (`console.log(dt)`, then remove it).
2. `Player` class. Draw it. Make it move. Clamp it.
3. `Item` class (the falling ball). Spawn one every second. Remove them when they fall off.
4. Collision between item and paddle. Score.
5. Lives, and the `"gameover"` state.
6. Pause.
7. `restart()`.

**Bonus ideas:**

- Items fall faster as the score goes up.
- Red items that you must **avoid**: catching one costs a life.
- Save a high score that survives restarts.

<details>
<summary>Answer</summary>

```js
const canvas = document.getElementById("game")
const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")

function random(min, max) {
  return Math.random() * (max - min) + min
}

// ---------- input ----------

const keys = {}

window.addEventListener("keydown", (e) => {
  keys[e.key] = true

  if (e.key.toLowerCase() === "p") {
    togglePause()
  }
  if (e.key.toLowerCase() === "r" && state === "gameover") {
    restart()
  }
})

window.addEventListener("keyup", (e) => {
  keys[e.key] = false
})

// ---------- classes ----------

class Player {
  constructor() {
    this.width = 100
    this.height = 15
    this.x = canvas.width / 2 - this.width / 2
    this.y = canvas.height - 30
    this.speed = 400
  }

  update(dt) {
    if (keys["ArrowLeft"]) this.x -= this.speed * dt
    if (keys["ArrowRight"]) this.x += this.speed * dt
    this.x = Math.max(0, Math.min(this.x, canvas.width - this.width))
  }

  draw(ctx) {
    ctx.fillStyle = "steelblue"
    ctx.fillRect(this.x, this.y, this.width, this.height)
  }
}

class Item {
  constructor() {
    this.radius = 12
    this.x = random(this.radius, canvas.width - this.radius)
    this.y = -this.radius
    this.speed = random(150, 250)
    this.done = false
  }

  update(dt) {
    this.y += this.speed * dt
  }

  draw(ctx) {
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(this.x, this.y, this.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    ctx.fillStyle = "orange"
    ctx.fill()
  }

  // treat the circle like a square for the collision check
  hits(player) {
    return this.x + this.radius > player.x &&
           this.x - this.radius < player.x + player.width &&
           this.y + this.radius > player.y &&
           this.y - this.radius < player.y + player.height
  }
}

// ---------- game state ----------

let player
let items
let score
let lives
let spawnTimer
let state

function restart() {
  player = new Player()
  items = []
  score = 0
  lives = 3
  spawnTimer = 0
  state = "playing"
}

function togglePause() {
  if (state === "playing") {
    state = "paused"
  } else if (state === "paused") {
    state = "playing"
  }
}

// ---------- update ----------

function update(dt) {
  if (state !== "playing") return

  player.update(dt)

  spawnTimer += dt
  if (spawnTimer >= 1) {
    items.push(new Item())
    spawnTimer = 0
  }

  for (const item of items) {
    item.update(dt)

    if (item.hits(player)) {
      score++
      item.done = true
    } else if (item.y - item.radius > canvas.height) {
      lives--
      item.done = true
    }
  }

  items = items.filter(item => !item.done)

  if (lives <= 0) {
    state = "gameover"
  }
}

// ---------- draw ----------

function drawMessage(text) {
  ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)"
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
  ctx.fillStyle = "white"
  ctx.font = "32px sans-serif"
  ctx.textAlign = "center"
  ctx.fillText(text, canvas.width / 2, canvas.height / 2)
}

function draw() {
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)

  player.draw(ctx)
  for (const item of items) {
    item.draw(ctx)
  }

  ctx.fillStyle = "black"
  ctx.font = "20px sans-serif"
  ctx.textAlign = "left"
  ctx.fillText(`Score: ${score}`, 10, 30)
  ctx.fillText(`Lives: ${lives}`, 10, 55)

  if (state === "paused") {
    drawMessage("Paused. Press P to continue")
  }
  if (state === "gameover") {
    drawMessage(`Game over! Score: ${score}. Press R`)
  }
}

// ---------- loop ----------

let lastTime = null

function loop(time) {
  if (lastTime === null) {
    lastTime = time
  }
  const dt = Math.min((time - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1)
  lastTime = time

  update(dt)
  draw()
  requestAnimationFrame(loop)
}

restart()
requestAnimationFrame(loop)
```

Things to notice:

- `restart()` is called once at the start **and** when you press R. No duplicated setup code.
- The loop starts only once and never stops. `state` decides what happens.
- Items are marked `done` and removed with `filter` afterwards, instead of being removed in the middle of the loop.
- `ctx.textAlign` is set back to `"left"` before drawing the score, because `drawMessage` changed it to `"center"`. Remember: the pen keeps its settings.

</details>
